source_text: Καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Εἰπὸν δὴ στάχυς. Οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον στάχυς· σημαίνει σέβηλα, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἄσταχυς. Οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον σεβήλω καὶ οὐκ ἐδύναντο τρανῶς εἰπεῖν σέδηλα. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ Ἑβραῖοι ἐτύγχανον, ἀλλὰ κατὰ συμμετρίαν βραχύτητι παρήλλασσον ἐν τῇ τῆς διαλέξεως προφορᾷ. Τὸ οὖν σύνθεμα ἦν σέβηλα, ὅπερ οἱ ἐπερωτώμενοι λέγοντες σεδήλω, ἠλέγχοντο οὐκ ὄντες τῶν οἰκείων τοῦ Ἰεφθάε, ἀλλὰ τῶν ἐπαναστάντων.
thought_title: The pronunciation test exposes the Ephraimites
orientation: Origen is explaining how the Gileadites used the word στάχυς as a password to identify Ephraimites by their mispronunciation.
pass_a_gloss: And they said to him: Say now 'ear of grain.' And they were saying 'ear of grain'; it means σέβηλα, which is 'ear of grain.' And they were saying σεβήλω and were not able to say clearly σέδηλα. For even if they happened to be Hebrews, yet by proportion they differed slightly in the utterance of the dialect. Therefore the password was σέβηλα, which those being questioned, saying σεδήλω, were convicted of being not of the household of Jephthah, but of those who had risen up.

lemmas.gloss: of those who had risen up

choices.why: Glossary requires 'ear of grain' for στάχυς; it is the test word spoken first.
Glossary requires 'ear of grain' for σέβηλα as the correct pronunciation; kept as σέβηλα in the gloss to preserve the pronunciation distinction.
Glossary requires 'mispronunciation' for σεβήλω; kept as σεβήλω in the gloss to preserve the pronunciation distinction.
Renders the genitive of belonging naturally; 'household' captures the sense of those belonging to Jephthah.

choices.english: of those who had risen up
choices.why: Renders the aorist participle of ἐπανίστημι as 'those who had risen up,' matching the context of the Ephraimites as rebels.

pass_b_english: And they said to him, “Say now ‘ear of grain.’” They would say “ear of grain”—that is, σέβηλα, which means an ear of grain. But the others would say σεβήλω, and they could not pronounce σέδηλα clearly. For even if they were Hebrews, they differed slightly in the brevity of their utterance in the dialect. So the password was σέβηλα, and when those who were questioned said σεδήλω, they were convicted of being not of the household of Jephthah, but of those who had risen up.

problems.why: Same concept (the test word) called both 'ear of grain' and 'password' without linking them explicitly.
problems.fix: Note that 'ear of grain' is the password being tested.

problems.quote: They would say "ear of grain"—that is, σέβηλα, which means an ear of grain. But the others would say σεβήλω, and they could not pronounce σέδηλα clearly.
problems.why: Three different Greek spellings appear with no clear mapping to who says what; sentence is confusing.
problems.fix: Clarify: correct form σέβηλα, mispronunciations σεβήλω and σεδήλω by Ephraimites.

fixed: The source says the password was σέβηλα, and those questioned said σεδήλω. The English already states this clearly: 'So the password was σέβηλα, and when those who were questioned said σεδήλω...' No edit needed.

The source has σέδηλα in the phrase 'οὐκ ἐδύναντο τρανῶς εἰπεῖν σέδηλα' (they could not say σέδηλα clearly). The English rendered this as σέδηλα, which matches the source. However, the confirmed problem suggests σέβηλα, but the source clearly reads σέδηλα here. The English is correct as is; no edit needed.
